sources.citation: Göksel, A. and Kerslake, C. (2025). Turkish: A Comprehensive Grammar. 2nd ed. London: Routledge. (1st ed. 2005.)
sources.used_for: Standard descriptive reference grammar of modern standard Turkish; source of the archiphoneme notation (-lAr, -(y)I, -DI) used in this guide; table of contents used to check the syllabus.
sources.access: In copyright. Publisher's table of contents opened 2026-11-12 (chapter level only); the text itself was not opened. Claims attributed to it in the dossier are marked (unverified) unless checked elsewhere. Unauthorised PDFs found in search were not used.

sources.citation: Lewis, G. L. (2000). Turkish Grammar. 2nd ed. Oxford: Oxford University Press. (1st ed. 1967.)
sources.used_for: Classic reference grammar with many literary examples; WALS cites the 1967 edition for most Turkish morphosyntax values.
sources.access: In copyright; not opened. Cited at second hand through WALS page references.

sources.citation: Kornfilt, J. (1997). Turkish. Descriptive Grammars series. London: Routledge.
sources.used_for: Linguist's descriptive grammar (syntax, nominalisation, case, voice); cited by WALS for many features.
sources.access: In copyright; not opened. Cited at second hand through WALS.

sources.citation: Underhill, R. (1976). Turkish Grammar. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.
sources.used_for: Teaching-oriented reference grammar; cited by WALS (word order, relative clauses, subordination).
sources.access: In copyright; not opened. Cited at second hand through WALS.

sources.citation: Ketrez, F. N. (2012). A Student Grammar of Turkish. Cambridge University Press.
sources.used_for: Modern student grammar; a further check on ordering and on spoken forms.
sources.access: In copyright; not opened.

sources.citation: Zimmer, K. and Orgun, O. (1999). Turkish. In Handbook of the International Phonetic Association, 154–156. Cambridge University Press. (First published in Journal of the International Phonetic Association 22, 1992.)
sources.used_for: Phoneme inventory and IPA values of Istanbul Turkish; WALS's phonology source.
sources.access: In copyright; not opened. Its values are cited at second hand through wpphon and WALS.

sources.citation: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (English edition): Turkish entries, declension and conjugation tables, suffix entries, Category:Turkish proverbs.
sources.used_for: Checking every inflected form (python3 tools/wikt.py <word> Turkish prints the full declension or conjugation table), suffix allomorph tables, informal spoken variants (e.g. yapıcam), proverbs.
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA). Opened throughout this session.

sources.citation: Türk Dil Kurumu (Turkish Language Association). Güncel Türkçe Sözlük (current Turkish dictionary), online.
sources.used_for: Official standard spelling, meanings, origin of loanwords, the accusative form of each noun (shows stem alternations such as kitap/kitabı) and pronunciation notes for long vowels and palatal consonants (hâl ha:li, kâr kâ:rı).
sources.access: Open online. The JSON lookup sozluk.gov.tr/gts?ara=<word> answered in this session; the HTML front page did not.

sources.citation: Dryer, M. S. and Haspelmath, M. (eds.) (2013). The World Atlas of Language Structures Online: Turkish (wals code tur).
sources.used_for: 154 typological feature values with their sources (word order, case, evidentiality, negation, copula), for the Compare screen and for points of disagreement.
sources.access: Open (CC BY 4.0). Language page and full value list opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Hammarström, H., Forkel, R., Haspelmath, M. and Bank, S. Glottolog 5.4: Turkish (nucl1301).
sources.used_for: Classification within Turkic (Oghuz), endangerment status, reference list.
sources.access: Open. Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Grambank: Turkish (nucl1301).
sources.used_for: Further typological values for the Compare screen.
sources.access: Open. Page opened 2026-11-12; the feature values load by script and were not extracted in this session.

sources.citation: Comrie, B., Haspelmath, M. and Bickel, B. (2015). The Leipzig Glossing Rules.
sources.used_for: Glossing conventions and standard abbreviations.
sources.access: Open. Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. Turkish phonology. English Wikipedia, revision 1384242891.
sources.used_for: Pointer to the phonetic literature (Zimmer and Orgun 1999, Göksel and Kerslake, Levi 2005, Kabak 2016): allophones of k g l, soft g, final devoicing, stress and its exceptions, harmony exceptions in loanwords.
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA); used as a pointer, not as authority. Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Levi, S. V. (2005). Acoustic correlates of lexical accent in Turkish. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 35(1), 73–97.
sources.used_for: The view that Turkish word accent is mainly a pitch accent.
sources.access: In copyright; cited at second hand through wpphon.

sources.citation: Kabak, B. (2016). Refin(d)ing Turkish stress as a multifaceted phenomenon. Paper, Second Conference on Central Asian Languages and Linguistics (ConCALL52), Indiana University.
sources.used_for: The view that Turkish has no unequivocal pitch-accent system.
sources.access: Cited at second hand through wpphon; not opened. Exact title (unverified).

sources.citation: Aksu-Koç, A. and Slobin, D. I. (1986). A psychological account of the development and use of evidentials in Turkish. In W. Chafe and J. Nichols (eds.), Evidentiality: The Linguistic Coding of Epistemology, 159–167. Norwood, NJ: Ablex.
sources.used_for: Evidential meaning of -mIş (direct versus indirect experience; surprise).
sources.access: In copyright; cited at second hand through WALS 77A and 78A.

sources.citation: Johanson, L. (2021). Turkic. Cambridge Language Surveys. Cambridge University Press.
sources.used_for: Place of Turkish in the Turkic family (cited in Glottolog's subclassification comment); background for tur-07-12.
sources.access: In copyright; not opened.

sources.citation: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Turkish translation (İnsan hakları evrensel beyannamesi), as distributed by the Unicode UDHR in Unicode project (udhr_tur.xml).
sources.used_for: Sample sentence in meta.json; reading tur-08-04 (Articles 1 to 3).
sources.access: Open; the UDHR may be freely quoted. File opened 2026-11-12. This is the older official translation, with Ottoman-era vocabulary (hür, haysiyet, içtimai).

sources.citation: Vikikaynak (Turkish Wikisource): Nasreddin Hoca fıkraları (Yorgan Gitti Kavga Bitti, rev. 170636; Tanrı Misafiri, rev. 142252; Ben Yapacağımı Bilirim, rev. 154565), each transcribed there from Bayraktar, Z. (2010), Mizah teorileri ve mizah teorilerine göre Nasreddin Hoca fıkralarının tahlili, doctoral thesis, Ege Üniversitesi.
sources.used_for: Readings tur-08-02 and tur-08-03 (anecdotes in -mIş narrative and -DI dialogue).
sources.access: Open. Pages opened 2026-11-12; Wikisource marks the anecdotes as anonymous folk works in the public domain. The wording of each retelling may be the thesis author's: quote one anecdote at a time, credit both, and keep to these short texts.

sources.citation: Yunus Emre (d. c. 1320). Aşkın Aldı Benden Beni (poem 4 in the Wikisource numbering), Vikikaynak, rev. 133694, with a second copy taken from Halk Edebiyatı Antolojisi on the same page.
sources.used_for: Capstone reading tur-08-08 (Old Anatolian Turkish in modernised Latin spelling).
sources.access: Public domain. Page opened 2026-11-12. The two copies on the page differ in wording and spelling (yanaram/yanarım, avunuram/öğünürem, stanza 5); the lesson must say which copy it follows.

sources.citation: Ömer Seyfettin (1884–1920). Kaşağı (short story, 1919). Vikikaynak, rev. 172873.
sources.used_for: Reading tur-08-06 (narrative past: -IrdI habitual, -Iyordu, -DI).
sources.access: Public domain (author d. 1920; first published 1919). Opened 2026-11-12. Wikisource gives a lightly modernised spelling; say so in the lesson.

sources.citation: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (1927). Nutuk, closing address 'Gençliğe Hitabe' (Address to the Youth). Vikikaynak, Nutuk/19. bölüm, rev. 174245.
sources.used_for: Reading tur-08-07 (formal 1920s prose with Ottoman vocabulary; cross-link to Ottoman Turkish, ota).
sources.access: Public domain (author d. 1938; published 1927). Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Vikipedi (Turkish Wikipedia), İstanbul, revision 38509756.
sources.used_for: Reading tur-08-05 (modern expository prose).
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA). Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Wikibooks contributors. Turkish (en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Turkish), revision 4460382.
sources.used_for: Checked for an open course; it is thin and partly unfinished. Not used as authority.
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA). Opened 2026-11-12.

sources.citation: Göksel, A. and Kerslake, C. (2005). Turkish: A Comprehensive Grammar. London: Routledge.
sources.used_for: Reference grammar for verifying suffix forms, suffix order, tense-aspect-mood and subordination.
